signals.title: CAD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + JPY Intervention & Data Outperformance
signals.text: CAD/JPY trades at 111.50 as the JPY outperformance theme dominates G10 FX. The 3.259% spread between the G10 leader (JPY) and laggard (CAD) is driven by a combination of confirmed Japanese intervention, record-high JGB yields, and surging manufacturing output, which grew at its fastest pace in 12.5 years (July). While CAD faces pressure from against the USD, JPY is benefiting from a 'strong positive' ESI of +22.9, signaling domestic data is consistently beating expectations. This fundamental shift is forcing an unwind of JPY shorts (COT LF net short -124,575), supported by a massive options market skew with USD/JPY 25d RR at -2.53. The pair sits below the USD/JPY SMA200 at 157.95, confirming a technical regime shift. Risk: BoJ holds a dovish stance at the next meeting, stalling the yield-driven JPY recovery.

signals.title: EUR/USD — COT Positioning + Fed Dissent + Vol Premium
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1535, holding above its SMA20/50 cluster (1.1429/1.1486) following the highest number of Fed dissents in a decade. Despite the recent breakout, COT LF positioning remains net short -92,930 (30.7% long), creating significant fuel for a short-squeeze if the Fed's hold is interpreted as a peak-rate signal. The options market is pricing in caution with a +2.6% Vol Risk Premium (IV 7.1% vs HV30 4.5%), suggesting traders are paying up for protection even as price action remains bullish. This divergence between net short positioning and price strength above SMA levels typically leads to trend extension as shorts capitulate. Watch for a close above the SMA200 at 1.1634 to confirm a long-term trend reversal. Risk: A hawkish repricing of the ECB hike bias removes the relative policy support.

signals.title: NZD/USD — COT vs OIS Divergence + ESI Strength
signals.text: NZD/USD at 0.5892 exhibits a sharp divergence between speculative positioning and fundamental momentum. COT LF specs are heavily net short -30,606 (9.7% long), while the RBNZ remains in a 'HIKING' cycle with a +33.4 ESI score, the second-highest in the G10. This creates an asymmetric risk profile where sustained data beats force an unwind of the crowded spec short. The pair is technically supported by the SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.5792–0.5826), currently trading above all three key averages. Retail sentiment is also at an extreme 75% short, aligning with institutional shorts and increasing the probability of a contrarian squeeze higher. Risk: RBNZ pauses the hiking cycle at the 2 Sep meeting, validating the spec short thesis.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Technical Breakout + Carry Support
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7034, successfully holding above the SMA50 (0.7013) and SMA20 (0.6978) after July manufacturing PMI returned to growth at 52.0. The 60bp AUD carry advantage (AONIA 4.35% vs SOFR 3.65%) continues to provide a structural floor for the pair during periods of normal volatility (VIX 16.0). COT positioning shows LF net long +23,616, suggesting institutional conviction in the AUD recovery is already established. While the AUD 25d RR shows a mild put skew (-0.66), the large +5.8% Vol Risk Premium indicates that downside protection is expensive relative to realized moves. Sustained trading above 0.7013 maintains the bullish technical bias toward the 1M high. Risk: A sharp drop in WTI oil prices spills over into broader commodity sentiment, weighing on AUD.
